thread:
andrew: FYI I rolled the CUDA 12 toolchain + driver 535 canary to 10 nodes in eu-west at 07:12UTC. Immediately saw init containers for gpuscheduler and nvidia-driver loop for some pods.

maria: Any crashlogs? are pods OOMing or stuck in init?

andrew: Not OOM. Containers stuck in Init with repeated lines: `NCCL WARN NET/Peer timed out` and `nvidia: failed to register iprovider: module version mismatch`. Example from node gpueu-07: `nv_peer_mlock: module has different kernel taint` followed by slow handshake retries.

li: That sounds like a driver vs kernel module ABI mismatch — maybe the host driver != kernel module in the container image. Which node image was used for the canary?

andrew: The canary used image: `redwood/gpu-runtime:cuda12-535.54.03-quant`. Host driver on eu-west is 535.43 (rolling kernel patch last week). We expected forward compat but this looks like a subtle rtld/taint issue.

sre-bot: ALERT: gpufleet provisioning queue increased by 38% in eu-west (07:14UTC). Pod pending time p95 -> 2m30s.

jen: A few customers reported inference latency spikes due to scheduling backpressure. Which pools are pinned to cuda12?

andrew: Only canary pool `dedicated-canary-eu` and a small on-demand queue. But the handshake hang causes long node churn which eats available capacity and pushes jobs to reserved fallback, increasing cost.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback requested by andrew at 07:18UTC.

maria: Please collect dmesg + `modinfo nvidia` output from affected nodes before rebooting. Also capture `lsmod | grep nvidia` and `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n50`.

andrew: Collected logs to /var/log/gpu-canary/gpueu-07.log and uploaded to S3 s3://redwood-ops/tmp/canary-1989991111/gpueu-07.log. Key snippets: `nvidia: kernel module 535.43 loaded, container module 535.54.03` then NCCL handshakes fail intermittently.

li: Ok, plan: 1) Pause toolkit rollout; 2) Drain canary nodes gracefully; 3) Roll back pod images to cuda11.8 runtime; 4) Open OS/kernel compatibility ticket with kernel team. Anyone object?

tim_oncall: I started draining nodes and scaled canary pool to 0 at 07:20UTC. Also opened INC-2026 for customer impact and PG-4231 for provisioning surge.

jen: Also note eu-west uses older kernel 5.15. We should gate the toolkit by kernel version in the deployment job. Add a predicate: `host_kernel >= 5.19` before auto-promote.

andrew: Agreed. Quick mitigation patch pushed to rollout pipeline to skip nodes where `uname -r` matches 5.15.*.

maria: For postmortem we should include cost delta: reserved fallback kicked in — estimate +13% GPU bill for the hour. Please attach billing spike to the incident.

li: Moving forward we should add an automated compatibility probe during provisioning: run small NCCL allreduce litmus between two GPUs on new nodes before marking them as available. If handshake fails mark node quarantined and pin to older runtime.

andrew: I'll draft the probe and PR the gating logic. Assigning myself and li.

ops-bot: ticket INC-2026 updated: status -> investigating.

jen: Thanks team. Keep notes short in the incident doc and add any kernel module mismatches found. :thumbsup:

andrew: Will follow up with PR link and timeline for re-try when we have kernel patch or unified driver build.
